In its quarterly results, Apple reported that R&D spending climbed to a record $11.73 billion, continuing the sharply accelerating trend of expenditures throughout fiscal year 2026. Here are the details.

Apple Increases R&D Spending

Last quarter, Apple reported R&D spending of $11.4 billion, a year-over-year increase of 34%.

On the company's earnings call, Tim Cook said Apple was "clearly investing more" and noted that R&D spending was "growing significantly faster than the company overall."

He went on to reiterate that R&D spending was "expanding significantly year over year," particularly when discussing Apple's AI investments. Apple CFO Kevan Parekh added that AI spending was incremental on top of Apple's normal product roadmap investments.

Apple today reported fiscal Q3 2026 results, with R&D spending reaching a record $11.73 billion, up 32% from the year-ago quarter, bringing Apple's total R&D spending so far in fiscal year 2026 to $34.04 billion.

For comparison, Apple's R&D spending for all of fiscal year 2025 was $34.55 billion. This means that with one quarter still remaining, the company has nearly matched its total spending for all of last year, and has already surpassed the full-year R&D spending for fiscal years 2024 and 2023.

Over the past few days, Wall Street has punished companies that announced accelerating AI-related spending without demonstrating equally clear short-term returns.

Alphabet's stock fell 7% after it raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast by $15 billion to between $195 billion and $205 billion. Meta's stock also dropped roughly 9% to 10% after it reported a 91% plunge in free cash flow while raising the lower end of its annual capital expenditure forecast to $130 billion.

Apple's stock is currently down about 4% in after-hours trading. The reaction could change again during the earnings call and when regular trading begins tomorrow.
